subject: Post-demo: ACME competitive bake-off plan and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: ACME competitive bake-off plan and next steps

Hi Sarah / Kunal —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps for the competitive bake-off so we can validate performance, cost, and integration effort against the hyperscalers and the incumbent solution you mentioned.

Key takeaways from the discovery:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost per 1M tokens while maintaining 95th-pct latency <= 250ms for single-turn prompts in your customer-facing chat flows.
- Important constraints: PII must not leave your VPC for regulated workflows; we need request-level audit logs and a SOC2 attestation.
- Workloads: 60% short chat prompts (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512) used in generate + streaming scenarios.
- Baseline: currently running on Hyperscaler-A managed endpoints (GPU A100 equivalent), average latency ~310ms, cost ~$1.25 per 1k tokens (including infra & egress).

Proposed bake-off plan (high level):
1) Test matrix: Redwood Hosted + Dedicated (pinned model) vs Hyperscaler-A managed endpoint vs Hyperscaler-B (vertex-style) — same model family where possible.
2) Scenarios: short chat, multi-turn with KV cache warm, streaming throughput (10 concurrent sessions), and long-form generation.
3) Success criteria:
   - Latency: 95th-pct <= 250ms for short chat
   - Cost: unit cost <= 0.6x current baseline for equivalent quality
   - Quality: top-line acceptance on 10-probe prompts (we'll run your eval set) — no more than 5% regression from baseline per metric (BLEU/ROUGE/likert where applicable)
4) Timeline: kickoff env setup by 2026-06-12, run tests 06/14-06/18, deliver report 06/21.
5) Owners: Redwood infra/test environment — Vanessa; Redwood evaluation + bench scripts — Marissa; Redwood commercial/contracting — Aditya.

Attachments: I attached a short comparison doc and a proposed MoP worksheet with test cases and owners.

Next steps:
- Sarah: confirm the eval set and whether we should include de-identified production traces (preferred).
- Kunal: confirm allowed test IPs for dedicated environment and whether you want VPC-private test instead of Hosted.
- Vanessa: can you provision a dedicated test pool and share creds?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscalers_20260610.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: acme-bakeoff-mop.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: ACME competitive bake-off plan and next steps

Thanks Aditya — this is excellent and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Eval set: we'll send a de-identified subset of production traces, about 2k examples across the length buckets you listed. We need to redact user IDs, but context and prompts will be intact.
- Network: we'd prefer VPC-private testing for the dedicated run (HIPAA-adjacent teams prefer no public egress).
- Timeline: 06/14-06/18 works, but could we extend run window by 2 days (until 06/20) in case of retries?

Also looping Tim from our consulting partner to help with evaluation metrics and quality acceptance criteria.

On owners: Sarah -> I'll own the eval set and access approvals; Kunal will handle IP/VPC peering details.

Looking forward to the plan and the attachments.

-Sarah
Director, AI Platforms
Acme Corp

Hi Sarah — great, thanks for the quick confirm. A few notes from the evaluation/bench perspective: 

- We'll run your 2k de-identified probes across the defined buckets and return per-test quality metrics (likert-style annotation for hallucination/severity plus automated signal). If you have existing labels/thresholds for what constitutes acceptable hallucination rates, please include them.
- For the quality acceptance test, we're proposing a 10% tolerance on subjective metrics and 5% on objective metrics relative to your current baseline (we can tighten if needed).
- Regarding model parity: we'll attempt to use the same open-family model versions across all platforms. When exact parity isn't possible, we'll pick closest-performance variants and note the divergence in the report.

I uploaded our standardized bench harness and scorer to the shared doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/shared/acme-bakeoff-plan (see folder 'bench-harness'). Vanessa — once you give the test creds, I'll kick off the first smoke runs and share the automation steps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi all — I'll provision the Dedicated test pool in your VPC and share a temporary peering token by EOD 2026-06-12. Notes: 

- Dedicated pool: 4x T4x2 nodes (est. baseline throughput for your workload). If you need larger capacity for the streaming stress test, let me know — we can burst to 8 nodes.
- Audit logging + KMS: we'll enable request-level logs and a customer-managed KMS key for test artifacts. Expect the audit logs to appear in the supplied S3 bucket (read-only for your team).
- Credentials: I'll send a service account key and an ephemeral password for the test harness. Please avoid storing creds in shared docs.

I'll attach the network checklist and the peering instructions here.

-Vanessa
